title: RAG vs Fine-tuning
description: Decision guide to help developers choose between Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Fine-Tuning.
name: RAG vs Fine-tuning
problem: Choosing the optimal method for adapting a pre-trained large language model to proprietary or domain-specific knowledge bases.

evaluation_criteria.description: How frequently the source information changes and whether the model must access updates in real time.
The degree to which the system must guarantee strict factual alignment and citation trace.
Upfront and ongoing computational resources required to deploy and maintain the adaptation pipeline.

options.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
strengths: Dynamic updates: Ingesting new documents requires zero training run-time cost.
Auditability: Output response statements can be explicitly linked back to retrieved context document chunks.
weaknesses: Context window constraints: Retrieving multiple blocks consumes prompt space.
Relies heavily on search index performance.
options.best_for: Applications with frequently changing external documents or data formats where factual grounding is critical.
options.avoid_when: The primary objective is teaching the model structural styling, task rules, or adapting to highly structured programming languages.

options.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
strengths: Custom style and tone adaptation: Excellent for adjusting task formatting.
Zero retrieval latency: The model stores parameters natively, saving database query steps.
weaknesses: Static knowledge: Updating training data requires rebuilding checkpoint runs.
High hallucination risk: Lacks direct citation verification capability.
options.best_for: Aligning tone, instructions, domain nomenclature, or optimizing latency by avoiding external retrieval pipelines.
options.avoid_when: The proprietary knowledge base updates hourly or requires exact mathematical proof matching.

comparison_table.Retrieval Cost: Low setup cost, variable per-token query costs.
comparison_table.Task Specialization: Limited by the pre-trained capability of the base model.

recommendations: Use RAG by default for knowledge retrieval tasks. Complement with Fine-tuning when model style, format constraints, or specific task instructions need adjustment.
use_cases: Enterprise search engine over internal wikis (RAG)
Converting user prompts into specialized DSL codes (Fine-tuning)
